title: Fuel, and supplies are sufficient till mid-May: CPC claims
byline: Amid public worries about fuel, Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) Managing Director Mayura Netthikumara said there is enough fuel, and supplies are safe until mid-May.

title: Sri Lanka among countries receiving UK prisoner transfers under formal agreements
byline: Sri Lanka has been identified as one of the countries to which the United Kingdom has transferred foreign national offenders under established Prisoner Transfer Agreements (PTAs), according to official UK Government policy.

title: Turkish Airlines increases flight frequency to Colombo amidst crisis in Middle East
byline: Amidst flight disruptions, Turkish Airlines has decided to increase the frequency of flights between Istanbul and Colombo by two additional flights per week to assist stranded tourists and enable travellers’ access to Sri Lanka, Daily Mirror learns.

title: Doctors want Saturday declared off-day amid fuel crisis
byline: The Association of Medical Specialists (AMS) has called for Saturday to be declared an off day, as the ongoing fuel crisis is placing severe strain on them.

title: Switch on fans when leaving pets at home, vets urge public
byline: As temperatures soar, veterinarians are warning that Sri Lanka’s animals are facing a silent heat crisis, with dehydration posing a serious threat to pets, farm animals and even birds.

title: Only rain gods can save Sri Lanka from power crisis
byline: Amidst disruption to global fuel supply, power generation is set to be a challenging task for Sri Lanka unless it rains sufficiently in the areas where the major hydropower reservoirs are located, an official said.

title: Hospital bed shortage may worsen amid ageing population, doctors warn
byline: Sri Lanka’s hospital system currently has nearly 85,000 beds, but the capacity may not be sufficient to meet future health demands, the Doctors’ Trade Union Alliance for Medical and Civil Rights warned, raising concerns over the growing elderly population and rising number of patients requiring specialised treatment.

title: Iran’s foreign minister says there are no negotiations with US
byline: Iran’s foreign minister says the country is not currently negotiating with the US to end the war and ’’does not intend’’ to do so.

title: Fertilizer shortage threatens Yala paddy cultivation: Farmers’ Union warns
byline: A severe fertilizer shortage could jeopardize paddy cultivation during the upcoming Yala season, National Farmers’ Union Chairman Anuradha Tennakoon warned.

title: Will study and come up with in Parliament on Iranian vessel issue: Ravi K
byline: Opposition MP Ravi Karunanayake, who was one-time Minister of Foreign Affairs, said today he will come up with a statement in Parliament after finding the real facts on the Iranian vessel issue.

title: Oil prices rise higher as Iran denies US talks, dimming deescalation hopes
byline: Oil prices have climbed higher amid fading hopes of deescalation in the Iran war following Tehran’s denial that talks with the United States are under way.

title: Russia’s Deputy Energy Minister arrives in Sri Lanka
byline: The Deputy Minister of Energy of Russia, Roman Marshavin, arrived in the country on a three-day official visit this morning.

title: Hormuz route opened for India: Iranian FM
byline: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Thursday said that they have permitted the passage of vessels for friendly countries, including India, through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: At least 24 people die after bus plunges into Bangladesh river
byline: A bus carrying about 40 people plunged into a river in central Bangladesh as it was driving onto a ferry, leaving at least 24 people dead, authorities said on Thursday.

title: Iran readies law to charge tolls in strait of Hormuz: ’ships must pay for security’
byline: Iran is preparing legislation to impose toll charges on vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, according to an Al Jazeera report citing Iranian news agencies Fars and Tasnim.

title: Tehran issues warning to regional neighbour if Iranian island occupied
byline: A senior official in Tehran has warned that intelligence reports suggest that “Iran’s enemies” ⁠are planning to occupy an Iranian island with support ‌from an unnamed country in the region.

title: Police warn public of fake discount airline ticket scams
byline: Sri Lanka Police have issued a warning to the public over fraudulent messages circulating on social media offering airline tickets at unusually low or special discounted rates.

title: 5,000 in final stage of kidney disease; 300 transplants in a year
byline: A total of 5,000 patients have been reported in the final stage of kidney disease, while 300 kidney transplants have been carried out in a year, the Health Promotion Bureau said.

title: Government of Sri Lanka has insulted Iran: Opposition
byline: The government of Sri Lanka has insulted Iran by denying the remark made by the Iranian Ambassador in Colombo that the vessel IRIS Dena received an official invitation from Sri Lanka to visit the island nation.

title: Central Bank resists rate hike
byline: The Central Bank left its key policy rate, the Overnight Policy Rate, unchanged at 7.75 percent yesterday, at its second policy meeting for the year.

title: Over 1,000 complaints over fuel QR Code fraud; several arrested
byline: The Digital Economy Ministry says it has received more than 1,000 complaints regarding fraudulent activities involving the use of other persons’ QR codes to obtain fuel.

title: Trump claims Iran proposed making him Supreme Leader: I said, ’No, thank you’
byline: US President Donald Trump on Thursday doubled down on his claim that he is in talks with Iran to end the nearly month-long war, even as Tehran flatly denied any negotiations were underway.

title: Over 6.2 Mn QR codes issued after reintroduction of National Fuel Pass System
byline: More than 6.2 million people have obtained QR codes after the reimposition of the QR-based National Fuel Pass system, Digital Economy Ministry Advisor Sumudu Rathnayaka said.

title: Three former DMT officials arrested over vehicle racket
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption arrested three former officials of the Department of Motor Traffic over their alleged involvement in an illegal vehicle registration racket.

title: Suresh Sallay returns to CID after hospitalisation
byline: Major General (Retired) Suresh Sallay, the former head of the State Intelligence Service, who had been admitted to the National Hospital in Colombo due to an illness related to his ear, was brought back to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) today after receiving treatment.

title: 24-hour help line launched for fishing and aquaculture fuel issues
byline: A 24-hour help line has been launched to assist the fishing sector and industries such as seafood processing and aquaculture with fuel supply issues.

title: ‘Ratama Ekata’ operation: 89 red-notice criminals to be repatriated
byline: Security forces in Sri Lanka are taking steps to repatriate 89 criminals who have been issued international red notices under the ongoing ‘Ratama Ekata’ national operation targeting drugs and organised crime.

title: Oil prices rise higher as Iran denies US talks, dimming deescalation hopes
byline: Oil prices have climbed higher amid fading hopes of deescalation in the Iran war following Tehran’s denial that talks with the United States are under way.

title: Hormuz route opened for India: Iranian FM
byline: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Thursday said that they have permitted the passage of vessels for friendly countries, including India, through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Iran readies law to charge tolls in strait of Hormuz: ’ships must pay for security’
byline: Iran is preparing legislation to impose toll charges on vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, according to an Al Jazeera report citing Iranian news agencies Fars and Tasnim.

title: Tehran issues warning to regional neighbour if Iranian island occupied
byline: A senior official in Tehran has warned that intelligence reports suggest that “Iran’s enemies” ⁠are planning to occupy an Iranian island with support ‌from an unnamed country in the region.

title: Bimal Rathnayake admits substandard coal imports
byline: Minister Bimal Rathnayake has acknowledged that substandard coal had been imported to Sri Lanka, stating that the company responsible has already paid fines amounting to up to USD 2 million.

title: CSE slides sharply amid renewed geopolitical uncertainty
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange witnessed a notable downturn on 26th March 2026, as renewed uncertainty surrounding developments in the Middle East weighed heavily on investor sentiment. Following two consecutive sessions of strong gains, the market reversed course, with selling pressure dominating throughout the session and driving the indices sharply lower.

title: Trump urges Iran to act quickly on ceasefire plan
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump warned Iran ​on Thursday to ’’get serious’’ about a deal to end nearly four weeks of fighting, after its foreign minister said Tehran was reviewing the U.S. proposal but that there were ‌no talks on winding down the war.

title: Russia agrees to supply refined fuel to Sri Lanka
byline: Russian Deputy Minister of Energy, Roman Marshavin, currently on an official visit to Sri Lanka, has agreed to supply refined fuel to the country following discussions with local authorities.

title: Registration of Persons Department halts all public services until further notice
byline: All public services at the Department of Registration of Persons will not be operational from tomorrow (27) until further notice, the Department announced today (26).

title: Trade Minister urges written request for butter import duty revision amid bakery price concerns
byline: Trade Minister Wasantha Samarasinghe today (26) requested bakery industry professionals to submit their proposals in writing for consideration of revising the import duty on butter, citing the impact of palm oil and butter prices on bakery products.

title: NIC one-day service suspended after system failure
byline: The computer system of the Department for Registration of Persons has reportedly crashed once again today (26), disrupting several essential public services.

title: Israel says strike killed Iran guards Navy Chief
byline: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz announced on Thursday that an Israeli airstrike had killed Alireza Tangsiri, commander of the Iranian Revolutionary Guards’ navy.

title: ’No exit strategy’: Germany criticises Israel-US war on Iran
byline: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius sharply criticised the US and Israel’s war on Iran on Thursday, saying the conflict lacks a clear strategy.

title: President to discuss fuel supply, energy security with Russian Deputy Energy Minister
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake is scheduled to meet visiting Russian Deputy Energy Minister Roman Marshavin this evening at the Presidential Secretariat, with discussions centering on strengthening bilateral cooperation in the energy sector, the President’s Media Division (PMD) said.

title: Fuel transport bowser owners to operate limited services from tomorrow
byline: The United Lanka Fuel Transport Bowser Owners Association (ULFTBOA) has decided to operate only a limited number of bowsers to transport fuel from tomorrow, the association announced.

title: Olympic women’s sport limited to biological females
byline: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) says eligibility will be determined by a ’’once-in-a-lifetime’’ sex test, which would prevent transgender women and those with differences in sexual development (DSD) who have gone through male puberty from competing.

title: National Namal Uyana declared a ‘National Heritage of Sri Lanka’
byline: The National Namal Uyana was officially declared a “National Heritage of Sri Lanka” for the first time at a ceremony held under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake at the Presidential Secretariat today (26), marking the 35th anniversary of the site’s establishment.

title: Rugby’s easter parade, sevens no longer an appetiser
byline: It looks as if the recent inter-club rugby Sevens tournament will mark the curtain-closer of the 2025-26 rugby season. Interestingly, there was a time in Sri Lanka’s rugby history when the inter-club rugby Sevens tournament was considered the curtain-raiser of the season.
